thread_text:
Ravi: Heads-up — onboarding run for tundra-embed-v2 int5 quant looks weird. recall@10 down ~6% on long-tail cohort compared to prod-embed-v3. UMAP shows cluster fragmentation for niche topics.
Anya: can you paste the benchmark table and config?
Ravi: Sure — config: `batch_size=128, seq_len=128, quant=per_channel_int5, backend=onnxruntime`. Results snippet:
```
Model                recall@10    recall@1    silhouette
prod-embed-v3         0.812        0.421       0.38
tundra-embed-v2-int5  0.756        0.402       0.22
```
Anya: silhouette drop is notable (0.38 -> 0.22). That matches the UMAP fragmentation.
Sam: Did you re-run with per-tensor quant? sometimes per-channel helps but int5 per-channel might be noisy for small layers.
Ravi: I tried per-tensor int5 earlier — recall@10 was slightly better (+1%) but silhouette still low. I can re-run per-channel int6 next.
Ciara: What about normalization pipeline? small changes there can flip long-tail semantics. Any preprocessing differences vs prod?
Ravi: Preproc is identical (lowercase, strip punctuation, whitespace collapse). We used same tokenizer and pooling (mean pooling) as prod.
Mike: Could be batchnorm/LayerNorm folding during ONNX export. Did you use `skip_layernorm_fold=false`?
Ravi: export args: `optimize=True, fold_layernorm=True` — maybe that fold introduced distribution shift under int5.
Anya: Try export with fold_layernorm=False and run a quick recall smoke on a 10k holdout (long-tail heavy).
Ravi: Running now. Also kicking off eval-bot to produce per-topic recall breakdown.
eval-bot: queued job 78932 for tundra-embed-v2-int5 per-topic recall breakdown. ETA ~7m.
Sam: Also run a small calibration set to compute per-dim scale factors before quantizing (staged calibration often helps odd low-bit formats).
Ciara: +1 on per-dim calibration. For int5 I usually clamp using 99.9th percentile rather than max. less noise.
Ravi: Good point. Will use percentile clamp and re-export with fold_layernorm=False.
Mike: If that helps, check kNN graph connectivity (k=10) and measure component counts — fragmentation would show as many small comps.
Ravi: Will add `components_count` to the eval.
eval-bot: job 78932 completed. Summary: long-tail cohort recall@10 = 0.744 (was 0.702 on earlier noisy run), silhouette = 0.29, components_count (k=10) = 42 vs prod 8. Full per-topic CSV: https://internal/redwood-evals/78932.csv
Anya: improvement, silhouette moved from 0.22 -> 0.29 after disabling LN fold and percentile clamp. Still worse than prod but closer.
Sam: Any latency or memory regressions with these changes? need to keep throughput assumptions.
Ravi: Latency +-1% and memory unchanged. int5 still saves ~18% memory over int8.
Ciara: Can we run a weighted recall where tail topics get higher weight? If product cares about niche clusters, that will show impact.
Ravi: I'll run weighted recall with tail weight x3. Kicking off now.
eval-bot: queued weighted-recall job 78933.
Ravi: Next steps: 1) rerun per-dim calibration + percentile clamp (done) 2) compare int6 per-channel export 3) run weighted recall and kNN connectivity 4) confirm export flags don't change runtime kernels.
Mike: Also add a short A/B to staging traffic (sampled) with fallback to prod if recall dips >5% in tail.
Anya: Nice. Ravi, drop the new CSVs in the embed-onboard folder and ping infra if you need a canary slice.
Ravi: Will do. Thanks all — will post results when int6 run completes. :thumbsup:
